title: Celestin's large band: bass, trombones and original members
summary: She recalls John Porter on bass/tuba, the trombonists Rousseau and Bill Matthews, Louie Barbarin on drums, and the four original members still living; others now play elsewhere.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: John Porter was the bass. He played tuba at that time.
And we had, let's see, I've mentioned the sax section, the trumpets, and the…
The trombone was, I think it was still August Russo.
I never knew him, I guess. I think when we interviewed Louie Nelson, who said he'd played with them for… No, no, that was mixed up. Louie Barberin?
That was the Sidney Desvinge band. Oh, yes. He was a big band.
No, Louie Barberin was our drummer then.
I was thinking trombones after Ridgely left. Do you remember who the trombones were?
Well, as I have foresaid, in the eight piece band we had Elvis Russo.
Oh, yes. Oh, that's right, sure.
Now, when we had the large band, we had Bill Matthews. Oh, Bill Matthews. Oh, sure. That's when he came. That's when he came in, in the big band. Yes, Bill Matthews.
And he stayed with him a long time then too.
He's one of the original members. Yes. Also, Louie Barberin and Narvin H. Kimball, we and myself.
I guess you all are about the last ones that are still…

We are the four original members. And a lot of them are dead and then some of them are in other groups. Other groups. For instance, Maya Kennedy and Clarence Hall is in Dave Bartholomew's band, but they are all original members also.
And with the large band. And we played… We kept busy day and night.
